AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `tools/fa-clip/` — the native macOS pasteboard helper (gh-2040): a plain
  `NSPasteboard` reader (`fa-clip <png|jpeg|tiff>` → bytes on stdout, exit
  2 = flavor absent), built by `scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` into the macOS
  CLI bundles (`bundle/bin/fa-clip`, per-arch) and shipped beside the `fa`
  binary — install.sh, install_local.sh and the self-update swap all copy
  it. The CLI resolves it relative to its own executable, never PATH; a
  missing/broken helper degrades to the named pasteboard-unavailable path.
  NEVER reintroduce the AppleScript/Apple Events clipboard transport
  (`osascript` is grep-gated out of `bin/` + `lib/src/cli/` —
  test/cli/fa_clip_helper_test.dart); the TCC «access data from other
  apps» dialog class must stay dead. macOS text reads stay on `pbpaste`
  (already prompt-free — documented split, gh-2040 AC4).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
  Flake intake consumes PR-dispatch runs only (gh-1537:
  `scripts/flake_watch.py` filters to `workflow_dispatch` events — the
  retired main trigger leaves SM validation dispatches and v* tag runs;
  a red tag run is a release-flow failure, triaged by daily-publish /
  ci-red-report, never quarantined as a flake). Dedup is per test name
  (the #1364 lesson): one test red across N runs files ONE issue.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs
  pre-merge in ci.yml's `pty-visual` leg — gh-1538 retired the nightly
  duplicate — and on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet in the pre-merge SM
  validation gate — every run that exists is a whole-tree
  `scripts/check_coverage.py 80` dispatch run; ci.yml has no
  `pull_request` trigger and no main runs since gh-1537, so the
  diff-coverage arm in `coverage-gate` is reserve for a future real PR
  trigger); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots
  (`lib`, `bin`, `flutter_app/lib`, `packages/*/lib`, `browser_ext/dart`)
  via `scripts/check_dup_cross_module.sh` — stage `dupx`, ONE jscpd
  invocation, marker-parity with the CI `guards` job (which also runs it
  for app-only PRs — cross-module clones are usually born app-side).
  Baseline 0.3013% of the combined ~283k lines, pinned 0.31 in
  `ci_fast_gate.sh` (ratchet — only tighten; the per-package gates above
  cannot see across module boundaries).
- CRAP ratchet (`crap4dart analyze`, tool pinned as
  `dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.15.0 <0.16.0"` — gh-1738
  superseded the old 0.11.0 bound: the root config's `gates.similarity`
  block ConfigExceptions on <0.15.0 parsers; gates/baselines need 0.15),
  one config per package, thresholds are the current per-package max —
  only down from here:
  - core (`crap4dart.yaml`, sources `[lib, bin]`): **12.0** (issue #1234:
    the named census offenders moved — CC-12 trio + readPasteboardImage
    16.32 split, the 0%-cov CC-3 quartet and the named CC-9 tier covered
    or split, `_listModels` covered — but the first whole-tree
    measurement showed the 8.0 repin unearned: 54 methods at 12.00
    (CC-3@0% tier + covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00. Threshold
    stays at the measured max; the tier is the next ladder card).
  - flutter_app (`flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`, sources `[lib]`,
    issue #433/#475): **30.0** — measured by the SAME pipeline the CI gate
    uses (the two `flutter-tests` shards emit `--coverage`; the
    `app-crap-gate` job merges the lcovs and runs the pinned analyzer —
    widget-test coverage differs from the core's dart lcov, E2).
  - The app ladder (follow-up cards, NOT this one): 2450 → 870 → 702 → 650
    → 380 → 272 → 210 (done: `JsAppEngine._faCall` 2450→6 via map
    dispatch, `patch` 94→19, `_tokenize` 70→18; issue #475:
    `wasm_shell_git.run` route-table + 51 golden tests, app `main()`
    boot-phase helpers, `wasm_shell` beasts `_grepBuiltin` 812→covered
    parse helpers, `_runPipeline` 702→210, `_runStage` 600→380,
    `_parsePrimary` 506→210; issue #558: the wasm_shell pipeline engine
    (`_runStage` 380→4, `_runPipeline` 210→4, `_evalExpr` 182→3); issue
    #559: the wasm_shell builtins (`_xargsBuiltin` 272→7,
    `_TestEvaluator._parsePrimary` 210→3, `_trBuiltin` 210→4,
    `_testBuiltin` 132→9, `_duBuiltin` 132→3, `_expandTrSet` 110→gone,
    `_tacBuiltin` 90→6, `_pipBuiltin` 72→3 — spec/table-driven parse
    helpers in `wasm_shell_builtins.dart` + tested exec halves) → next
    milestone 210-class (`GemmaService.chatStream` — gh-2004 since removed, `_statBuiltin` 156,
    wide_layout 156 pair) → … → **40**, each step "fix the code, then
    lower the threshold" — never lower first.
  - Guards (`scripts/check_crap_guards.py`): README badge == config
    threshold for BOTH packages, generated-exclude parity between the
    two configs, and `--only-down` (a PR that raises any threshold vs
    the merge base is rejected in CI).
- Max 2800 lines per `.dart` file (crap4dart `loc` gate, issue #1234 —
  generated output excluded in the gate configs; `*.g.dart` exempt).
- CI layout: `changes` (path filter) → parallel `static`, `test-core`
  (3 duration-balanced shards, `scripts/test_shards.json`, rebalanced
  weekly from junit durations; shard jobs emit junit-shard-N artifacts and
  `shard_files.py` bin-packs manifest-missing new test dirs at runtime),
  `coverage-gate`, `guards`, `flutter-tests` (ubuntu; goldens stay
  host-locked in build-macos.yml) → one aggregate `Quality gate`
  required check, plus `step-timings` (per-step duration telemetry) and a
  `watchdog` (>2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out PR leg gets ONE
  empty-commit retrigger — never `gh run rerun`, which reallocates into
  the same degraded runner pool). `perf-gate` (issue #303) folds the #262
  DoD `dart test --tags perf` trajectory gate into the aggregate for
  trajectory-touching PRs. Issue #551 adds the `integration-mock` leg to
  the aggregate for `test/integration/**` PRs (no-key legs via
  MockLlmServer); the tag-only `integration` job is just the llm provider
  smoke and `publish` waits on it. Issue #1267 N1 adds the
  `flutter-app-exzone` leg: it runs the macOS exclusion-zone family
  (`flutter_app/test/apps/` — JS-engine tests the ubuntu leg skips via
  `native_test_guard.dart`, plus `flutter_app/lib/apps/` + `lib/src/js_ext/`
  are the code that surfaces there) on macos pre-merge, closing the
  nightly-only gap the #1309 escape rode. Under this repo's dispatch-only
  CI the leg is path-blind: ci.yml has no `pull_request` trigger (SM
  `workflow_dispatch` validation is the PR gate), so the leg runs in every
  SM validation dispatch (gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom); the
  `flutter_app/lib/apps/**`/`lib/src/js_ext/**`/`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`
  path set in the `changes` job only narrows a future real `pull_request`
  trigger. Tag/schedule/release runs skip it — gh-1538 retired the
  nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg is the macOS
  coverage for the JS-engine surface (with gh-1537 there are no main ci
  runs at all — the SM validation dispatch is the single test gate).
  **Nightly (gh-1538) is builds + integration-only**: `nightly.yml` keeps
  the release-mode build matrix (all store/desktop targets) + PTY/CLI
  integration (full real-provider suite with secrets, un-quarantined per
  gh-1199); unit shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd and the duplicated
  cli-visual / flutter-app-macos legs moved out as pre-merge-gate
  duplication. `coverage-gardener.yml` measures the only-up CLI
  coverage weekly and files an ai-teammate "raise coverage to X" issue —
  the baseline itself only moves through a reviewed PR (issue #927).

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a

+    # and Android APK/AAB legs add an explicit cross-target invocation
+    # beside their NDK pre-install. Idempotent + a clean no-op when the
+    # package graph carries no sqlite3.
+    - name: Prewarm sqlite3 native-assets (bounded retry, gh-2072)
+      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
+      shell: bash

+      run: |

+        # `dart <path>` inside a package whose graph carries sqlite3
+        # would build that package's OWN native-assets hooks first — the
+        # exact single-attempt download this step exists to bypass. A

+        # builds no hooks; it only reads the target packages' configs as

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          # gh-1522: the committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
          # stamp the PR bundle's version.txt from git describe (short sha
          # on shallow checkouts) so `fa --version` stays meaningful.
          version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)
          version="${version#v}"
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own GREEN push run IS
    # the gate (the dedupe lookup fires only on conclusion == "success") —
    # the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh, whose
          # conventional-commit fallback reads commit MESSAGES since the
          # previous tag — same reason release-macos fetches full
          # (gh-1477: blobless, never historical file blobs). Whichever
          # matrix leg wins the create race must be able to produce the
          # full curated body.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
      # the TAG is the version (the retired flow compared tag vs pubspec
      # because a bot commit bumped the file; that commit path is gone).
      # Guard the placeholder here and stamp the bundle version from the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder
        # Explicit bash: the default shell on Windows runners is pwsh and
        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash
        run: |
          placeholder=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          if [ "$placeholder" != "0.0.0-dev" ]; then
            echo "::error::committed pubspec.yaml version is '$placeholder', expected the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (gh-1522) — a hand-bump desyncs the tag-derived builds. Revert pubspec.yaml."
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}

runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret
      # when available.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
        with:
          targets: android
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
=== iOS job 836-870 ===
      - name: Assert TestFlight version floor
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bundle install
          bundle exec fastlane ios assert_version_floor

      # Issue #726 (run 35491603044): pub has no retry for its git-dep
      # mirror clones — one flaky TCP connect to github.com:443 ("Failed
      # to connect ... after 11155 ms") failed the whole leg with no
      # retry. The bounded retry + deterministic-skew fail-fast now lives
      # in the shared composite action every enforce-lockfile pub get in
      # the repo rides (gh-1310; pinned by test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_
      # test.dart).
      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # #1331 size diet: js_widget_runtime declares `test/assets/` as a
      # package asset DIRECTORY, so its 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture
      # rides every app bundle. Nothing in the app references it (the #1227
      # mac pass verified by grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib and
      # the bundled JS apps — only the package's own tests load it, and
      # those live in the package repo). Removing the file is safe: the
      # pubspec declares the directory, not individual files.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
        with:
          targets: arm64-ios
      - name: Prune never-loaded package test fixture (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

=== flutter-pub-get action full ===
name: 'Flutter pub get (enforced lockfile, bounded retry)'
description: >-
  The ONE sanctioned flutter_app dependency-resolution step:
  `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` with the #726 bounded retry. pub
  has no retry for its git-dependency mirror clones (flutter_js,
  flutter_js_widget_runtime) — one transient "Connection reset by peer" on
  github.com:443 failed the whole leg (#726 on the iOS release leg; gh-1310
  on ci.yml build-macos, where the v1.0.516 lockfile refresh cold-missed
  the flutter-action pub cache and forced fresh clones exactly when a
  release lands). Deterministic pubspec/lockfile skews (gh-1299: a release
  commit that bumps the version without regenerating flutter_app/
  pubspec.lock) fail identically on every attempt — the loop detects the
  "Unable to satisfy" signature and fails fast instead of burning ~30s per
  red leg and blaming the network (PR #1268 review thread 3). Guarded by
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart: no workflow run-step may resolve
  flutter_app itself.

inputs:
  working-directory:
    description: 'Directory holding the pubspec.yaml to resolve.'
    required: false
    default: flutter_app

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile (bounded retry, #726)
      working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      env:
        # Git-dep clones must never hang a leg on a credential prompt.
        GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        LOG_FILE="$(mktemp)"
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
          if flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_FILE"; then
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 0
          fi
          # A pubspec/lockfile skew is deterministic — retrying cannot
          # fix it, so fail fast instead of burning ~30s per red leg and
          # blaming the network (PR #1268 review thread 3).
          if grep -qE 'Unable to satisfy .* using .*pubspec\.lock' "$LOG_FILE"; then
            echo "::error::$PWD/pubspec.lock is out of sync with $PWD/pubspec.yaml — regenerate it (cd $PWD && flutter pub get) and commit; not retrying a deterministic skew"
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
            echo "::error::flutter pub get failed after 3 attempts — the runner's network to pub.dev/github.com is unhealthy"
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::warning::flutter pub get failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 15s"
          sleep 15
        done

    # gh-2072: prewarm the sqlite3 package's native-assets hook cache — the
    # hook downloads `libsqlite3.<abi>.<os>` from GitHub releases at build
    # time in a single attempt with no status check, and one transient
    # `504 Gateway Time-out` error page red'd four legs and the aggregate
    # Quality gate at v1.0.697 (a tree that had passed the same legs hours
    # earlier). Every flutter leg resolves flutter_app THROUGH THIS ACTION,
    # so the prewarm here covers the whole flutter class with one edit;
    # root-package (`dart test`) legs carry the explicit invocation pinned
    # by test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart. Host-auto targets: iOS
    # and Android APK/AAB legs add an explicit cross-target invocation
    # beside their NDK pre-install. Idempotent + a clean no-op when the
    # package graph carries no sqlite3.
    - name: Prewarm sqlite3 native-assets (bounded retry, gh-2072)
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      shell: bash
      env:
        PREWARM_PACKAGE_ROOTS: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        DART_BIN="$(command -v dart || true)"
        if [ -z "$DART_BIN" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot locate dart on PATH — the sqlite3 native-assets prewarm needs the Dart SDK"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Copy the script OUT of the workspace before invoking it: plain
        # `dart <path>` inside a package whose graph carries sqlite3
        # would build that package's OWN native-assets hooks first — the
        # exact single-attempt download this step exists to bypass. A
        # script outside any package resolves no package config and
        # builds no hooks; it only reads the target packages' configs as
        # data.
        SCRIPT_COPY="$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm.dart"
        cp scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart "$SCRIPT_COPY"
        ARGS=()
        for root in $PREWARM_PACKAGE_ROOTS; do
          ARGS+=(--package-root "$root")
        done
        # auto = the host platform: covers `flutter test` legs and the
        # desktop build targets (macos/linux/windows rows build no web or
        # cross targets here). Android/iOS device targets are provisioned
        # by the explicit cross-target invocations in the build legs.
        ARGS+=(--targets auto)
        ARGS+=(--attempts 4)
        if ! "$DART_BIN" "$SCRIPT_COPY" "${ARGS[@]}"; then
          echo "::error::sqlite3 native-assets prewarm failed — gh-2072: the sqlite3 hook downloads prebuilt binaries mid-build with no status check and no retry; one transient GitHub error page reds the leg and the aggregate Quality gate. Inspect the attempts above; the wiring guard is test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart."
          exit 1
        fi

# pr-2078: gh-2072 [ci-red] v1.0.697 failed

## Description

Closes #2072
### Root Cause
The `sqlite3` package's native-assets build hook downloads its prebuilt `libsqlite3.<abi>.<os>` binary at **build** time with a single attempt and no HTTP status check (`sqlite3` 3.7.0, `hook/compile/description.dart`, pinned by `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` via `flutter_agent_memory`). During the v1.0.697 run the runner egress answered `504 Gateway Time-out` for release-asset downloads; the hook saved the 92-byte HTML error page as the library and its own sha256 check threw (`Bad state: Hash of downloaded file … bef140a1a96994029153dca8c00b1750b9a5a764fb9db2dc68d7bb40e8a29e8a` — the exact hash of the 504 page, identical across four legs). Four CI legs + the aggregate Quality gate red'd on a tree that had passed the same legs hours earlier.

### Fix
- `scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart`: resolves the installed `sqlite3` package from each package config, parses its pinned `asset_hashes.dart` (single source of truth — windows assets have no `lib` prefix: `sqlite3.x64.windows.dll`), downloads the requested prebuilt libraries with bounded retry, HTTP-status checks, sha256 verification and atomic writes into the hook's own reuse cache (`<root>/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-<hash8>/`), so the hook never touches the network.
- `.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm`: composite action (`targets`: `auto` / `android` / `arm64-ios` / explicit), wired before the first build/test step in every hook-building leg, and appended to the shared `flutter-pub-get` action so every flutter leg is covered by one edit.
- Explicit cross-target invocations: `ci.yml` build-android (APK ABIs) + build-ios (`arm64-ios`), `build-mobile.yml` (4 legs), the `nightly.yml` release matrix (`sqlite3_targets` per row; desktop rows covered by the central `auto` prewarm, web builds no code assets).
- `test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart` pins the wiring map, ordering (prewarm before any hook-building step) and explicit targets, in the style of the gh-1655 NDK guard.

### Test Coverage
- `test/scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm_test.dart` — 54 tests: 504-then-200 retry proof, status-blind and hash-mismatch rejection, corrupt-cache repair, clean no-op without sqlite3, unknown-target failure, windows/apple asset-naming pins — **PASSED**
- `test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart` + full ci-guard family — 264 tests — **PASSED**
- `bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook` — GATE_RESULT_PLACEHOLDER
- End-to-end proof on the real toolchain: prewarm → hook reused the cached file (frozen mtime untouched, zero network); control run without cache re-downloaded at the same path.

The flutter-pub-get embedded prewarm failed → reds a leg that (per their own analysis) needs NO prebuilt. This is the **fail-closed design**: when the prewarm can't download (sustained egress outage), legs that would otherwise build fine (web!) go red. The old behavior: hook downloads at build time... for web builds, would the hook run? Per the PR author's own matrix comment: "web builds no code assets" — so WITHOUT the prewarm, the web leg is immune to the 504. WITH the prewarm wired unconditionally into flutter-pub-get, the web leg now FAILS when the prewarm can't reach github. **That's a regression: the fix converted an immune leg into a dependent one.** Evidence: "Build web (debug)" failed at 07:59:27 with `PREWARM FAILED — flutter_app: 1 of 1 targets failed... 504` — while the same leg on the old tree was immune (their own comment in nightly.yml: "web builds no code assets — nothing to prewarm"). BLOCKING-class: the prewarm's hard-fail makes previously-immune legs (web, and any leg where hooks wouldn't actually download) fail during egress outages. This is a design finding — the prewarm should be `continue-on-error: true` (best-effort: if it can't prewarm, fall back to the hook's own behavior — which is the status quo ante) OR skip on download failure with a warning. The hook's single-atempt download is no worse than prewarm failing after 4 attempts... actually the hook would then re-atempt its own download at build time — possibly recovering if egress recovered. Hard-failing the prewarm forecloses that. This is a strong IMPORTANT/BLOCKING. Given it actually red'd the Build web leg THIS run — I'll rate it 🚨 BLOCKING (red gate, plus a regression for legs that were previously immune).

🚨 **BLOCKING: the AC3 coverage map omits the `binaries-pr` and `binaries` jobs — the exact legs that failed on this PR's own CI run with the bug this PR fixes**

The map pins 19 ci.yml jobs but not `binaries-pr` (ci.yml:4842, 5 matrix legs, required "Binaries smoke gate" context) nor the release-path `binaries` matrix (ci.yml:4034). Both jobs resolve the root package and then run `dart build cli` (`dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart` at ci.yml:4889 and ci.yml:4148) — a hook-building step per this guard's own `hookBuildingSignatures`.

This is not hypothetical: on this PR's head commit (run 42582141385, commit de262fc9), the `Binaries (PR)` ubuntu-x64 and macos-x64 legs failed with exactly the sqlite3 hook 504 this PR exists to prevent — `Unexpected response code: 504 Gateway Time-out` from `PrecompiledFromGithubAssets._fetchFromSource` inside `dart build cli`, exit 255 — and the aggregate `Binaries smoke gate` red'd with them. No prewarm step appears anywhere in those legs' logs. The PR description's claim "wired before the first build/test step in every hook-building leg" is false for the legs that carry the same `dart build cli` this PR wires into `fa-aot-build`.

Fix:
1. Add `- uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm` after the `dart pub get` step in **both** `binaries-pr` and `binaries` (default `auto` targets are correct — host builds only).
2. Add both jobs to `sqlite3PrewarmJobs` so the count assertions keep them wired ("cover the whole release-blocking class, not just the four legs that happened to lose the dice" — this map's own stated contract).

🚨 **BLOCKING: prewarm runs BEFORE `dart pub get` in this job — guaranteed red on every run**

The step order here is:

1. Native-assets hook cache restore
2. **sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm** ← line 1205
3. `dart pub get` ← line 1206
4. `dart build cli`

The prewarm script reads `<root>/.dart_tool/package_config.json` and **hard-fails when it is missing** (`scripts/sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart`: "package_config.json not found — run pub get before the prewarm"). On a fresh checkout there is no package config until step 3 runs, so this step fails structurally — not transiently.

It already did: on this PR's own run (commit de262fc9), the **AOT fa binary** leg failed at 07:54:02 with

```
PREWARM FAILED — .: ./.dart_tool/package_config.json not found — run pub get before the prewarm
```

Fix: move this `- uses:` line to **after** `- run: dart pub get` (line 1206) and before `dart build cli`.

Note the guard test cannot catch this: it only checks "prewarm before the first hook-building step", and `dart pub get` is deliberately not a hook-building signature. See also the AC-hardening comment on the guard test.

🚨 **BLOCKING: cross-target prewarm reads the wrong package root — `.` has no package config in this job**

This explicit invocation relies on the action's `package-roots` default (`.`), but this job's only dependency resolution is `flutter-pub-get` with `working-directory: flutter_app` — there is **no root `dart pub get`** anywhere in the build-android steps. So the script looks for `./.dart_tool/package_config.json` at the repo root, which never exists here, and hard-fails.

It already did, twice, on this PR's own run (commit de262fc9):

- **Build Android APK (debug)**, 07:59:09: `PREWARM FAILED — .: ./.dart_tool/package_config.json not found — run pub get before the prewarm` → exit 1 → leg red (the embedded flutter-pub-get prewarm above it had already succeeded for `flutter_app` at 07:58:39 — the wiring, not the network, is what failed).
- **Build iOS (debug, unsigned)**, 07:59:04: same error (same cause, `targets: arm64-ios` at ci.yml:3039).

Fix for both cross-target invocations (`build-android` here and `build-ios` at ci.yml:3039):

```yaml
- uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
  with:
    targets: android
    package-roots: flutter_app   # ← the root whose package config actually exists here
```

(The same `package-roots: flutter_app` correction applies to all four explicit invocations in build-mobile.yml — see that file's comment.)

🚨 **BLOCKING: all four explicit prewarms in this workflow use the default `package-roots: '.'` — none of these jobs has a root package config**

Same defect as ci.yml's build-android/build-ios legs, now in build-mobile.yml at four sites:

- line 190 — `build-android` (`targets: android`)
- line 443 — `build-android-apks` (`targets: android`)
- line 599 — `test-android-emulator` (`targets: android`)
- line 865 — `build-ios` (`targets: arm64-ios`)

Every one of these jobs resolves dependencies exclusively through `./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get` (which runs `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` inside `flutter_app/` — that is the action's own `working-directory` default and the guard `test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` forbids workflows from resolving flutter_app any other way). None of them runs a root `dart pub get`, so `./.dart_tool/package_config.json` never exists and the prewarm script exits 1 with

```
PREWARM FAILED — .: ./.dart_tool/package_config.json not found — run pub get before the prewarm
```

These legs did not run in this dispatch (build-mobile is manual/nightly), so the breakage is latent — but it is structural, not transient: the first nightly/manual run after merge reds all four legs.

Fix: add `package-roots: flutter_app` to each of the four `with:` blocks.

(Sweep suggestion: extend the AC5 branch of `test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart` so any prewarm with explicit `targets:` must also declare `package-roots:` explicitly — that would have pinned this.)

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: unconditional prewarm breaks the documented out-of-scope fastpass in this job (and two siblings)**

Every setup step in this job is conditional on `needs.changes.outputs.core/shared` — checkout, setup-dart, pub cache, and `dart pub get` are all skipped on out-of-scope PRs so the leg stays green via the "Scope fastpass" step ("out-of-scope → green in seconds"). The new prewarm step (this line) has **no `if:`**.

On an app-only or docs-only PR at the next release-pending dispatch this leg goes red by construction:

- `test-core` (this job, shards 0–3): checkout AND setup-dart are skipped → the local composite action can't even resolve (`./.github/actions/...` is not on disk) → all four required shard contexts fail.
- `guards` (ci.yml:1764, same insertion): checkout/setup-dart DO run there (`core||shared||app||docs`), but `dart pub get` is gated `core||shared` only — skipped for app/docs PRs → the prewarm dies on the missing package config. The job itself documents the invariant this violates, four lines above the pub get: *"on a skipped (app-only) PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127"* — the prewarm has exactly the same dependency set (dart + package config).
- `model-switch-reg` (ci.yml:1939, same insertion): same shape as guards.

Fix: give each of the three inserted steps the same `if:` as the pub get it depends on:

```yaml
- uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
  if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
```

This run's dispatch happened to be core-in-scope, so the failure is latent here — but it will red the required contexts on the first out-of-scope PR, which is precisely the case the fastpass design exists to keep green.

🚨 **BLOCKING: the integration (tag-only provider smoke) job has NO `dart pub get` before this prewarm**

Step order in this job: checkout → setup-dart → hooks cache → **prewarm** → `dart test --tags "integration && llm"`. There is no explicit pub-get step at all — `dart test` would do an implicit one, but the prewarm runs first and requires `./.dart_tool/package_config.json` to already exist. It doesn't on a fresh checkout, so the script exits 1:

```
PREWARM FAILED — .: ./.dart_tool/package_config.json not found — run pub get before the prewarm
```

This job is the ONLY tag-only LLM leg and `publish` waits on it (`needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok` gating) — i.e. every `v*` tag push / release publish would red here, structurally, on every run.

Fix: add `- run: dart pub get` immediately before this prewarm step (the other root-package legs — `usage-fold`, `perf-gate`, `dep-audit`, `js-ext-integration` — all already have it; this one is the exception).

🚨 **BLOCKING: the prewarm fails closed, converting legs that were IMMUNE to the 504 into prewarm-dependent legs — Build web proved it on this very run**

This `exit 1` makes the prewarm a hard gate on every leg that carries it. But a prewarm can only *help* legs that actually build sqlite3 hooks; on legs with no hook to protect it is pure added risk. Concretely:

- **Build web (debug)** failed on this PR's run (07:59:27): `PREWARM FAILED — flutter_app: 1 of 1 targets failed for flutter_app (first: x64-linux: download failed after 4 attempts: HTTP 504 ...)`. Web builds no code assets — the PR's own analysis says so (`nightly.yml`: "web builds no code assets — nothing to prewarm"). At v1.0.697, during the same egress 504 storm, the web leg stayed **green** (only the four hook-building legs red'd). This PR turned an immune leg into a failing one.
- The same storm red'd `usage-fold`, `build-web` (embedded prewarm), `flutter-tests` shard 0 and `terminal-visual` on this run — the 504 outage lasted 5+ minutes while the bounded retry covers ~35s (4 attempts, 5/10/20s backoff), so for hook legs the fix shifts the failure earlier but for this window does not prevent it (the android leg surviving on attempt 4 shows it does help for short blips).

Recommended fix (best-effort semantics, matching gh-1655/gh-1757's "pre-install is an optimization, not a gate" spirit):

```yaml
- name: Prewarm sqlite3 native-assets (bounded retry, gh-2072)
  continue-on-error: true
  ...
  if ! "$DART_BIN" "$SCRIPT_COPY" "${ARGS[@]}"; then
    echo "::warning::sqlite3 native-assets prewarm failed — falling back to the hook's own (single-attempt) download"
```

With `continue-on-error: true` the outcome strictly dominates today's: hook-building legs lose nothing (the hook keeps its own download path when the prewarm can't run), and legs with no hook (web, static, dep-audit) regain their immunity to egress outages.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the guard passed 41/41 on this tree while the actual CI wiring fails at six points — three AC blind spots**

I ran `dart test test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart` on this PR's head: **41/41 green**, yet the same commit red'd CI at:

1. `binaries-pr` + `binaries` — not in the map at all (hook 504, exit 255, this run)
2. `fa-aot-build` — prewarm placed **before** `dart pub get` (missing package config, this run)
3. `build-android`/`build-ios` — default `package-roots: '.'` where only flutter_app is resolved (missing package config, this run)
4. `build-mobile.yml` ×4 — same wrong package root (latent)
5. `test-core`/`guards`/`model-switch-reg` — unconditional prewarm vs conditional checkout/pub-get (latent)
6. `integration` — no pub get before the prewarm at all (latent, blocks publish)

The guard validates presence, order-vs-hook-building-step, and explicit targets — but:

- **No AC asserts prewarm AFTER the job's pub get.** `dart pub get` is deliberately excluded from `hookBuildingSignatures`, so `fa-aot-build` (prewarm → pub get → build) passes even though the script hard-fails without the pub get first. Add: for each mapped job, the first prewarm index must be greater than the first `dart pub get` index (or an explicit `package-roots` must be present whose path the job actually resolves).
- **AC5 checks `targets` but never `package-roots`.** Every build-android/build-ios/build-mobile step sailed through with the broken `.` default. Add: a step with explicit cross-targets must declare `package-roots:` and the value must match where the job runs pub get.
- **The map's completeness claim is unenforced for binaries.** The AC3 count assertion only compares against the map itself; a job missing from the map is invisible. Add `ci.yml/binaries-pr` and `ci.yml/binaries` (both run `dart build cli` — they match this file's own `hookBuildingSignatures`).

The guard's header says "a future leg must red HERE, not silently re-enter the download roulette" — today the roulette is still spinning while the guard applauds. The wiring fixes above must land together with these AC additions, or the next refactor re-introduces this silently.

💡 **SUGGESTION: per-attempt `HttpClient` is never closed on the failure path, and no attempt has a request timeout**

In `downloadVerified` the client is created inside the retry loop (line 403) and `client.close()` only runs on the success path (line 433) — after a non-200 or a hash mismatch the client leaks until process exit. Harmless for one file, but `targets: android` × N packages can stack several per leg.

Also, neither the request nor the body read (`await for (final chunk in response)`, line 420) has a timeout: a connection that hangs open (no 504, just a stalled socket) parks the step until the *leg's* wall-clock timeout kills it — the bounded-retry budget never engages. Two small fixes:

```dart
final client = HttpClient()
  ..findProxyFromEnvironment = ... // unchanged
  ..connectionTimeout = const Duration(seconds: 30);
...
request.timeout = const Duration(seconds: 120); // per-attempt budget
// and on the failure paths:
client.close(force: true);
```

(or hoist one client out of the loop and close it in a `finally`). Add a `SocketException`-style hang to the fixture tests if you take the timeout.

💡 **SUGGESTION: this prewarm protects nothing on this leg — wrong package root, wrong package**

Two mismatches:

1. With the default `package-roots: '.'` the script reads the **repo root's** package config and downloads `libsqlite3` into the **repo root's** `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/...` cache. But the only Dart code built in this leg runs under `browser_ext/dart` (`cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && dart test`), and hooks_runner caches are per-package-root — the root cache this step fills is never read here.
2. `browser_ext/dart` doesn't depend on sqlite3 at all (nothing in its pubspec/lockfile), so its graph can never trigger the sqlite3 hook in the first place — there is nothing on this leg to protect.

Net effect: every headless-suite run pays up to ~1 minute of download (plus the retry window on a bad-egress day) for a file nothing consumes. Either drop this line, or — if the intent is future-proofing — point it at the package that matters, after its pub get:

```yaml
- name: Dart unit tests (browser_ext/dart)
  run: cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && dart test
```

with the prewarm removed from this leg entirely (a `package-roots: browser_ext/dart` invocation would be a clean "no prewarm needed" no-op today — not worth a step). Also update the AC3 map entry for `browser-ext.yml/headless-suite` accordingly.

## Review summary — PR #2078 (gh-2072 sqlite3 prewarm)

**Verdict: `REQUEST_CHANGES`** — the prewarm script and its 54 tests are genuinely solid (FIPS-vectored hand-rolled sha256 justified by the out-of-package execution model, 504-then-200 retry proof, corrupt-cache repair), but the CI wiring reds the PR's own run at four points, breaks four more paths by construction, and the new guard test passes **41/41 green** over all of it (I ran it on this head to prove the blind-spot claim, not assume it).

Key findings (12 threads + 2 digest lines):
- 🚨 **7 BLOCKING** — `binaries-pr`/`binaries` legs unwired (they failed THIS run with the exact hook 504 the PR fixes, exit 255); `fa-aot-build` prewarm before `dart pub get`; `build-android`/`build-ios` + `build-mobile.yml`×4 reading `package-roots: '.'` where only `flutter_app` is resolved (2 red this run: 07:59:09/07:59:04); unconditional prewarm vs conditional checkout/pub-get in `test-core`/`guards`/`model-switch-reg` (violates the invariant documented at ci.yml:1749); `integration` job with no pub get at all (blocks `publish` on every v* tag); fail-closed prewarm converting previously-immune legs into prewarm-dependent ones (`Build web` red'd this run — web was green during the v1.0.697 storm).
- ⚠️ **1 IMPORTANT** — guard-test AC blind spots (no prewarm-after-pub-get check, no `package-roots` check, binaries jobs absent from the map).
- 💡 **4 SUGGESTIONS** — no per-attempt HTTP timeout/client leak; browser-ext step protects nothing (wrong package root, no sqlite3 in that graph); retry budget ~35s vs the multi-minute outage observed this run; ~35-line bash duplication already drifting between the two actions.
- 🪶 **2 NITs (digest)** — dead `sqlite3_targets: auto` matrix rows in nightly; `GATE_RESULT_PLACEHOLDER` left unsubstituted in the PR description.
